title: Neon Quiz Sprint
premise: A retro-futuristic runner dashes down a neon lane, jumping over spike hazards and stopping at recurring quiz gates that must be cleared to continue the run.
interaction_model: Single-button endless runner movement with modal two-choice quiz answers between action segments.
objective: Survive as long as possible, build distance, clear quiz gates, and increase speed without hitting spikes or answering incorrectly.
progression: The run starts at a moderate pace, continuously increases score over time, triggers a mandatory quiz gate every 1000 score units, and rewards correct answers with bonus score, a token, and higher speed.
theme: Arcade neon sprint blended with light edutainment math-checkpoint gameplay.
mood: Energetic, flashy, arcade-like, lightly tense, and playful.
likely_audience: children or younger players comfortable with simple arithmetic
players who enjoy endless runners with a small quiz twist
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core loop is endless runner plus quiz gate because the update loop explicitly pauses for math events every score threshold.
High confidence that spikes are the only direct action hazard in the current implementation.
Moderate confidence that character choice is primarily cosmetic, although the two characters do use different body dimensions and may slightly affect collision feel.
Moderate confidence that the intended audience includes younger players due to simple arithmetic prompts and approachable controls.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser game called "Neon Quiz Sprint," a neon-soaked endless runner with a quiz-gate twist. The player chooses between two retro arcade runner avatars on a start screen, then begins auto-running across a chrome-lit futuristic lane while a synthy action loop plays. During live play, the only movement input is jump: tapping, clicking, pressing Space, or pressing Up should make the runner vault over pink spike hazards scrolling in from the right. The world should feel like an endless side-scrolling sprint, with the character fixed near the left side, a glowing sunset, moving clouds, a parallax city skyline, a purple checker track, scanline overlays, and bright arcade HUD panels. Show distance as the main score and also track tokens earned from quiz clears. Every time the run reaches a regular milestone, pause gameplay and open a bold centered quiz gate modal that presents a simple arithmetic question with exactly two large answer buttons. If the player picks the correct answer, play a rewarding success sound, briefly show a celebratory reaction visual, grant one token, add a score bonus, increase run speed, and resume the sprint. If the player answers wrong, end the run immediately just like a hazard collision. Hitting any spike should also cause instant game over with failure feedback and a restart option. Keep the loop fast, readable, mobile-safe, and short-session friendly: run, dodge, clear quiz gate, accelerate, repeat until failure. The tone should feel energetic, colorful, slightly tense, and playful, mixing classic endless-runner reflexes with lightweight math challenge pacing.
